findings.evidence: `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Irreducible.lean:73`: `theorem IsIrreducible.nontrivial {ρ : Representation k G V} (h : ρ.IsIrreducible) : Nontrivial V`, proved by exactly the `IsSimpleModule.nontrivial` + `asModuleEquiv.symm.toEquiv.nontrivial` chain repeated at Basis.lean:226-229. It is already used this way at `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Continuous/Unitary/Equivalence.lean:88`.
findings.fix: Replace lines 224-229 with `have _ := (models i).isIrreducible.nontrivial`. Better: factor the whole `hdim` (lines 222-232) as `IrrepModel.dim_pos : 0 < m.dim` next to `IrrepModel` in `PeterWeyl.lean`, since positivity of a model's dimension is a fact any later block argument needs.
findings.issue: The `hdim` block re-derives `Nontrivial` from `IsSimpleModule.nontrivial` and `asModuleEquiv` by hand (lines 224-229), reinventing an existing repo lemma.

findings.evidence: Lines 217-246 depend on `i` only through `models i`; they mention the skeleton `h` nowhere. The remaining proof (248-262) is the span induction and is genuinely one-off.
findings.fix: Extract `hblock` as a named lemma in the `ContRepresentation` section, e.g. `inner_matrixCoeffLp_eq_zero_of_inner_characterLp_eq_zero` taking one model (or one irreducible unitary `π` with an orthonormal basis) and the vanishing pairing, and leave the skeleton proof as `hblock` + the span argument.
findings.issue: `eq_zero_of_forall_inner_characterLp_eq_zero` runs ~51 lines of script (212-262), of which lines 217-246 are a self-contained per-model statement — orthogonality to the character of one irreducible kills all of that block's matrix coefficients — inlined as a `have`.

findings.evidence: Lines 94-106 use neither `f` nor `hf`; only the calc at 107-110 does. The identity is the standard covariance `(π)_{π h v, π h w}(g) = (π)_{v,w}(h⁻¹ g h)` and will be wanted again for any further central/Fourier argument.
findings.fix: State it as its own lemma (e.g. `ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_map_map` next to the other `matrixCoeffLp` algebra in `Compact/MatrixCoefficient.lean`, or above `inner_matrixCoeffLp_map_map` here); `inner_matrixCoeffLp_map_map` then reduces to the three-line calc at 107-110.
findings.issue: `key : matrixCoeffLp π hπ (π h v) (π h w) = conjLpₗᵢ 𝕜 h⁻¹ (matrixCoeffLp π hπ v w)` — the conjugation-covariance of a matrix coefficient, and the entire a.e. content of the surrounding proof (lines 94-106) — is hidden in a `have`. It is a statement about `matrixCoeffLp` alone, with no class function in sight.

summary: Proofs are readable and free of undocumented defeq manipulation, but three pieces of reusable reasoning are buried inline: an existing repo lemma is re-derived by hand, a per-model completeness step is inlined into a 50+-line proof, and the conjugation-covariance identity for matrix coefficients is hidden inside a `have`.
